title: Adaptive hydraulic provider lifecycle zero-waste audit
motivation: The strict Richards candidate shows material lower-level speed gains, while the production-shaped serialized Reference-floor timing is only equivocal (median adaptive/analytical ratio 0.984431). Code inspection shows adaptive representation acquisition is repeated on every physical advance.
code_authority_observations: fmr_serialized_advance calls bind_b110_adaptive_hydraulic_provider on every prescribed-head adaptive advance.
b110_adaptive_hydraulic_cache_t%get_or_build returns a cache hit through intrinsic assignment table=self%entry(i)%table.
Because the table contains allocatable x,z,dzdx,logk arrays, that cache-hit assignment deep-copies the representation rather than lending immutable cached storage.
The analytical fallback inside the adaptive provider remains step-duration dependent, so table lifetime and step binding must be separated rather than blindly persisting the whole current provider.
question: How much avoidable cost is caused by per-advance adaptive representation acquisition/deep-copy, and can immutable cached representation ownership be separated from cheap step-duration binding without changing hydraulics or routing semantics?

required_checks: prove repeated cache hits occur across repeated physical samples
measure warm bind/cache-hit cost independently from table build
measure representation copy/allocation contribution where possible
retain exact existing F-AHL27 fidelity and fallback semantics

repair_target.step_dependent_state: only authoritative analytical fallback binding and other genuine timestep-dependent state
repair_target.cache_hit: no deep copy of support arrays

decision_rule: Repair only if repeated representation acquisition is demonstrated and the no-copy lifecycle preserves bitwise or frozen-gate-equivalent hydraulics while reducing measured bind/application overhead.
